scope: Proposition 2.2 (Regeneration law) of the manuscript “A directional zero–one law for finite-range-dependent random environments” (preprints/A-directional-zero-one-law-for-finite-range-dependent-random-environments-October-5-2026/directional-zero-one-finite-range.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 220 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 010edc479fd82038), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a normalized real direction v and suppose pv > 0. (i) Under the raw law P0, on {supn h(Xn) = ∞} there is a cut almost surely. (ii) Under b Pv, there are infinitely many cuts. With time zero counted as an initial boundary, the relative marked words between successive boundaries are independent and identically distributed. Their common law νv assigns mass νv({γ}) = W(γ) (2.7) to each regeneration word γ. These finite words concatenate to the entire conditioned walk. (iii) Under the raw law, conditional on any realized prefix through the first cut, the translated suffix has law b Pv. This assertion is restricted to the event that a cut exists.
